title: Resilience Garden Initiative — roadmap and care tasks
body:
Purpose and elevator pitch:
The Resilience Garden Initiative is a cross-functional program to cultivate, measure, and scale service-level objectives (SLOs) across core product surfaces using a lightweight, operational-first approach. Think of SLOs as garden plots: small, tended areas that together make the whole product resilient. This doc outlines the 12-week roadmap, explicit care tasks for each plot, owners, and acceptance criteria.

Scope (what this initiative will do):
- Baseline and map service dependencies for critical customer paths (API ingest, generation, latency-sensitive endpoints).
- Define and land first-wave SLOs for 6 service groups: API gateway, request router, inference runtime, KV-cache, logging pipeline, metrics ingestion.
- Implement cross-team alerting/urgency rules and an operational playbook for error budget consumption > 30% in a rolling week.
- Run three reliability experiments (prefix caching rollouts, request-priority routing, degraded-model fallback) and measure impact on SLO and cost.
- Create a repeatable onboarding kit for new teams to adopt SLOs in 2 sprints.

Out of scope: full company-wide SLO rollout (phase 2), infra capacity purchases, billing model changes.

Guiding principles:
- Start small: measure one customer-critical flow end-to-end before adding more SLOs.
- Actionable SLOs: each SLO must map to a playbook and at least one runbook owner.
- Observable and testable: all SLOs require dashboards, synthetic checks, and one chaos/experiment.
- Minimize noise: aim for alerts that require human action less than 1/week per team.

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Program lead: Maya Chen (eng-sre) — program cadence, cross-team coordination, exec updates.
- Product sponsor: Aisha Gomez (product-console) — prioritization of customer flows, acceptance.
- Metrics & dashboards: Ravi Patel (observability) — dashboard templates, synthetic checks.
- Runtime experiments: Liam O'Connor (serving-runtime) — experiment design and rollout.
- Incident runbooks & training: Sofia Rivera (platform-engineering) — playbook authoring and exercises.
- Team leads (API, Router, Runtime, Cache, Logging, Metrics) — SLO owners and on-call alignment.

12-week high-level timeline (by sprint):
- Weeks 1–2 (Discovery): dependency mapping, owner alignment, choose 2 customer-critical flows to instrument; create baseline dashboards.
- Weeks 3–4 (Define): write SLO proposals (SLO name, target, measurement window, error budget policy), review with product & support, finalize playbook skeletons.
- Weeks 5–6 (Implement): instrument metrics, deploy synthetic checks, create dashboards, wire alerts to pagers/Slack channels.
- Weeks 7–8 (Experiment run 1): prefix/KV caching rollout to 10% of traffic for one flow; measure latency and error SLOs.
- Weeks 9–10 (Experiment run 2): graded degraded-model fallback for runtime; measure user-visible errors, latency regressions, cost delta.
- Weeks 11–12 (Handoff & onboarding): retro, refine playbooks, produce onboarding kit and 2-sprint checklist for new teams.

Milestones and acceptance criteria:
- M1 (end Week 2): end-to-end dependency maps for chosen flows, owners confirmed. Acceptance: maps reviewed by team leads and product.
- M2 (end Week 4): SLOs defined and approved. Acceptance: SLO templates complete, playbook stub exists, product sign-off.
- M3 (end Week 6): metrics + synthetic checks live. Acceptance: dashboards show baseline, synthetic tests run every 5m with recorded history.
- M4 (end Week 8): experiment 1 complete. Acceptance: clear experiment report showing delta on latency and SLO burn rate.
- M5 (end Week 10): experiment 2 complete + fallback policy validated. Acceptance: rollback/runbook validated and on-call drills executed.
- M6 (end Week 12): onboarding kit published. Acceptance: two non-SRE teams complete onboarding checklist in pilot.

SLO templates (example fields):
- SLO id: slo.api.ingest.critical-path
- Objective: 99.9% requests with latency < 350ms over 30d (rolling).
- Measurement: service-level request success = status 2xx and latency <350ms.
- Window: 30d rolling.
- Burn policy: alert at 30% error budget in 7d, page at 50% in 7d.
- Owner: api-team lead (name + email).
- Runbook: link, immediate mitigations, rollback steps, stakeholder contact list.

Operational playbook highlights (short):
- When error budget >30% in 7d: create "SLO Watch" channel, run triage, apply mitigation (rate limit non-essential routes, enable degradation path), update exec brief.
- When error budget >50% in 7d: page on-call, run incident template with SLO-tracking column, consider auto-fallback to smaller model or cached result.
- Post-incident: write remediation doc, add preventative test to synthetic suite.

Experiment designs (quick notes):
- Prefix/KV cache experiment: rollout in three waves (1%, 10%, 50%) with canary metrics; measure token-level cost,  p99 latency, cache hit rate, and SLO burn.
- Priority routing: route low-priority background requests to lower-cost capacity; measure throughput, effect on high-priority latency.
- Degraded-model fallback: when runtime latency > threshold, serve cheaper quantized variant; measure user-visible accuracy regressions and error rate.

Risks and mitigations:
- Alert fatigue: mitigate by raising alert thresholds and introducing composite signals that combine error budget + user impact.
- Measurement drift: validate metrics definitions with synthetic tests and log sampling; run weekly checks against raw traces.
- Cross-team coordination gaps: enforce stakeholder sign-offs at milestone gates; weekly sync with clear async notes.

Communication cadence and artifacts:
- Weekly working sync (30m) — program lead + team leads; publish notes to Confluence.
- Biweekly exec readout (15m) — highlights, one experiment result, any escalations.
- Shared sprint board: Jira epic SRE-412 contains tasks and owners.
- Slack channels: #resilience-garden (async updates), #slo-watch (alerts).

Onboarding kit (deliverables for other teams):
- 1-page SLO quickstart (what an SLO is and how to pick a target).
- Dashboard + synthetic check template (Grafana/Prometheus queries).
- Playbook checklist (playbook template, runbook entries).
- Mini-experiment guide (how to run a 2-week canary experiment safely).

Quick checklist for first 6 teams adopting SLOs:
- Agree on the critical user flow.
- Map dependencies and list owners for each component.
- Complete SLO template and get product sign-off.
- Deploy synthetic check and baseline dashboard.
- Define error budget policy and notification routing.
- Run a small chaos or degradation exercise and document results.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- SLO enforcement model: should we block deployments when the team is in a depleted error budget? (ops change request needed)
- Default SLO targets for non-customer-facing infra (internal ingestion pipelines).
- Cost vs reliability guardrails for experiments — who signs off on expected cost delta limits?

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Finalize two customer-critical flows to instrument (API-ingest, chat-generate) — owner: Aisha — due 2026-05-14.
- Kick off dependency mapping workshops with owners (2x 90m sessions) — owner: Maya — schedule by 2026-05-15.
- Provision temporary dashboard space and synthetic test runner for proofs-of-concept — owner: Ravi — done by 2026-05-18.

Notes to self / rough ideas (working):
- Consider an "SLO health" micro-badge for teams on internal directory — gamify adoption.
- Add a column to PRs that notes whether the change affects an SLO-bound path.
- Explore using historical A/B traffic splits to simulate degraded-model fallback before production rollout.
